instructions:
Below is a draft essay. Revise it so that it reads as if a US grade 8 student wrote it in class for a timed writing test. Keep the position it argues and keep it at about 271 words. The file must contain only the revised essay.

Draft:

Dear Principal Harmon,

I am writing about the cell phone policy you are reconsidering. I believe Policy 1, which lets students use phones at lunch and during free time but keeps them off in class, is the better choice.

My first reason is safety and family logistics. Many of us ride the bus, walk home, or stay late for practice. Last month my rehearsal ended forty minutes early, and without my phone I would have waited outside in the dark until my mother's shift ended. A total ban does not remove these situations. It just sends every one of them through the front office, which already has enough to do.

Second, a ban would be very hard to enforce. Students will still bring phones, only now they will hide them in backpacks and bathrooms, and teachers will spend class time searching instead of teaching. Policy 1 gives a rule most students will actually follow, because it is fair. When people get a reasonable freedom at lunch, they have less reason to sneak a look during math.

Third, Policy 1 teaches something. In a few years we will have jobs where nobody takes our phones away, and we will have to decide for ourselves when to put them down. School is a good place to practice that with clear limits and real consequences.

I understand the worry about distraction, and I share it. That is why phones should be off, not just silenced, during class, with confiscation for anyone who breaks the rule.

Please choose Policy 1. It protects learning time without treating every student as a problem.

Sincerely,
A ninth-grade student
